## 1. Classification of Rigid-Body Planar Motion

A **rigid body** is an idealized solid in which the distance between any two points remains strictly constant ($\|\mathbf{r}_{B/A}\| = \text{constant}$) regardless of the forces or moments applied. Planar (2D) rigid-body motion is classified into three foundational regimes:

:::: {.pillar-grid}

::: {.pillar-card style="border-top: 4px solid #2563eb;"}
[Regime 1 • Zero Rotation ($\omega = 0$)]{.pillar-tag style="color: #2563eb;"}

[Pure Translation]{.pillar-title}

Every line segment on the body remains parallel to its original orientation. Because $\mathbf{r}_{B/A}$ is constant in both magnitude and direction, $\dfrac{d\mathbf{r}_{B/A}}{dt} = \mathbf{0}$, so **every point shares the exact same velocity and acceleration**:
$$\mathbf{v}_B = \mathbf{v}_A, \qquad \mathbf{a}_B = \mathbf{a}_A$$
:::

::: {.pillar-card style="border-top: 4px solid #059669;"}
[Regime 2 • Fixed Pivot ($O$)]{.pillar-tag style="color: #059669;"}

[Pure Rotation About a Fixed Axis]{.pillar-title}

Every point $P$ at radial distance $r$ from fixed pin $O$ sweeps a circular arc $s = r\theta$. Linear speed scales with radius ($v = \omega r$), while acceleration splits into tangential (speed change) and normal (centripetal) components:
$$a_t = \alpha r, \qquad a_n = \omega^2 r = \frac{v^2}{r}$$
:::

::: {.pillar-card style="border-top: 4px solid #4338ca;"}
[Regime 3 • Translation + Rotation]{.pillar-tag style="color: #4338ca;"}

[General Planar Motion]{.pillar-title}

The body simultaneously translates and rotates (such as a connecting rod, sliding ladder, or rolling wheel). We analyze velocity via **Vector Superposition** ($\mathbf{v}_B = \mathbf{v}_A + \boldsymbol{\omega}\times\mathbf{r}_{B/A}$) or via the **Instantaneous Center ($IC$)**.
:::

::::

:::: {.thought-box}
:::: {.example-split}
::: {}
**💡 Thought Experiment: Sliding a Box Across a Lab Bench (Pure Translation)**

Imagine a heavy wooden box resting on a flat, horizontal lab bench. You mark Point $A$ at the top-left corner and Point $B$ at the bottom-right corner, then push the box straight across the table without tipping.

Because the box is rigid and does not rotate, the relative position vector $\mathbf{r}_{B/A}$ has constant magnitude and constant angle. Taking the time derivative of $\mathbf{r}_B = \mathbf{r}_A + \mathbf{r}_{B/A}$ yields $\mathbf{v}_B = \mathbf{v}_A + \mathbf{0}$ and $\mathbf{a}_B = \mathbf{a}_A$. Every point on a translating body shares the exact same kinematics!
:::

## 2. General Planar Motion: Algebraic Vector Method vs. Geometric ICZV Method

By **Chasles' Theorem**, any rigid body undergoing general planar motion can be treated at a specific microsecond as rotating purely about an invisible, temporary stationary point called the **Instantaneous Center of Zero Velocity ($IC$ or $ICZV$)** where $\mathbf{v}_{IC} = \mathbf{0}$.

```{=html}
<table class="method-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="width: 18%;">Feature</th>
<th style="width: 41%;">Method 1: Relative Velocity Equation (Algebraic / Vector)</th>
<th style="width: 41%;">Method 2: Instantaneous Center of Zero Velocity (Geometric / ICZV)</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Core Principle</strong></td>
<td>Superposition of translation of reference point <em>A</em> plus pure rotation of <em>B</em> relative to <em>A</em>.</td>
<td>Pure rotation of the entire rigid body about a temporary stationary pivot point <em>IC</em> where <strong>v</strong><sub>IC</sub> = <strong>0</strong>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Governing Equation</strong></td>
<td><strong>v</strong><sub>B</sub> = <strong>v</strong><sub>A</sub> + (<strong>&omega;</strong> &times; <strong>r</strong><sub>B/A</sub>)</td>
<td><em>v<sub>A</sub> = &omega; &middot; r<sub>A/IC</sub></em> &nbsp;and&nbsp; <em>v<sub>B</sub> = &omega; &middot; r<sub>B/IC</sub></em> &nbsp;(Scalar)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Primary Strengths</strong></td>
<td>Systematic, purely algebraic, extends directly to 3D kinematics and relative acceleration equations.</td>
<td>Fast, visual, bypasses cross-product sign errors, and reveals velocity distributions across linkages immediately.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Key Limitations</strong></td>
<td>Cross products with <strong>i</strong>, <strong>j</strong>, <strong>k</strong> unit vectors require careful bookkeeping of signs and quadrant angles.</td>
<td><strong>Strictly valid for velocity only!</strong> Because <strong>a</strong><sub>IC</sub> &ne; <strong>0</strong> in general, <em>IC</em> cannot be used for accelerations.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
```

### Four Geometric Rules for Locating the Instantaneous Center ($IC$)

:::: {.rule-grid}

::: {.pillar-card style="border-top: 4px solid #4338ca;"}
[Case 1 • Non-Parallel Velocity Directions]{.pillar-tag style="color: #4338ca;"}

[Intersection of Perpendiculars]{.pillar-title}

Because every point moves tangent to a circle centered at $IC$, the radius vector $\mathbf{r}_{P/IC}$ is always perpendicular to $\mathbf{v}_P$. Draw a line $\perp$ to $\mathbf{v}_A$ through $A$ and a line $\perp$ to $\mathbf{v}_B$ through $B$; their intersection is $IC$.
:::

::: {.pillar-card style="border-top: 4px solid #0284c7;"}
[Case 2 • Known Velocity $\mathbf{v}_A$ & Angular Speed $\omega$]{.pillar-tag style="color: #0284c7;"}

[Radial Distance Along the Normal]{.pillar-title}

If you know the velocity vector $\mathbf{v}_A$ of a single point and the body's angular velocity $\omega$, construct a line perpendicular to $\mathbf{v}_A$ at $A$ and measure distance $r_{A/IC} = \dfrac{v_A}{\omega}$ toward the side that produces the correct rotational sense.
:::

::: {.pillar-card style="border-top: 4px solid #059669;"}
[Case 3 • No-Slip Contact (Wheels, Gears, Cords)]{.pillar-tag style="color: #059669;"}

[Point of Tangency is $IC$]{.pillar-title}

When a rigid wheel rolls without slipping on a stationary ground (or unwinds from a taut, stationary vertical cord), the point of contact $C$ (or tangency $E$) has zero instantaneous velocity ($\mathbf{v}_{IC} = \mathbf{0}$).
:::

::: {.pillar-card style="border-top: 4px solid #d97706;"}
[Case 4 • Parallel Velocities ($\mathbf{v}_A \parallel \mathbf{v}_B$)]{.pillar-tag style="color: #d97706;"}

[Similar Triangles Construction]{.pillar-title}

When $\mathbf{v}_A$ and $\mathbf{v}_B$ are parallel and perpendicular to line $AB$, $IC$ lies on line $AB$ at the intersection with the line joining the tips of $\mathbf{v}_A$ and $\mathbf{v}_B$: $\omega = \dfrac{|v_A - v_B|}{d_{AB}}$ (same sense) or $\omega = \dfrac{v_A + v_B}{d_{AB}}$ (opposite sense).
:::

## 3. Four-Mechanism Interactive ICZV Telemetry Lab {#iczv-simulator}

Select any of the **four classic engineering mechanisms** below and click **▶ Play Motion** (or drag the sliders) to observe how the Instantaneous Center ($IC$) and velocity vectors evolve in real time:

1. **Slider-Crank Piston Engine (Horizontal $x$-Motion):** Crank $OA$ rotates at constant speed $\omega_{OA}$, driving connecting rod $AB$ and forcing piston $B$ to reciprocate horizontally along the cylinder axis. At $\theta = 90^\circ$ and $270^\circ$ the two perpendiculars become parallel ($IC \to \infty$), placing rod $AB$ in **instantaneous pure translation** ($\omega_{AB} = 0$)!
2. **Constrained Sliding Ladder / Bar ($AB$):** Top collar $A$ slides vertically down the wall while bottom end $B$ slides horizontally along the floor, with $ICZV$ tracing a circular arc of radius $L$ in the first quadrant.
3. **Rolling Wheel Without Slipping:** The ground contact point serves as $IC$, doubling the speed at the top crown ($v_T = 2v_G$).
4. **Unwinding Disk on a Taut Cord:** The disk unwinds downward along the vertical rope fixed at $D$ while rotating counter-clockwise about tangency point $E$ ($IC$), with roving rim point $P(\phi)$ and spokes visibly rotating and translating downward.

```{=html}
<script>
let icMode = 'piston';
let icAnimId = null;
let isPlaying = false;
let animAngle = 45;
let wheelXOffset = 0;
let spoolYOffset = 0;

function syncFromSliders() {
  animAngle = parseFloat(document.getElementById('slParam3').value);
  drawICCanvas();
}

function setICMode(mode) {
  icMode = mode;
  const modes = ['piston', 'bar', 'wheel', 'spool'];
  const ids = {piston: 'btnModePiston', bar: 'btnModeBar', wheel: 'btnModeWheel', spool: 'btnModeSpool'};
  modes.forEach(m => {
    const el = document.getElementById(ids[m]);
    if (el) {
      el.style.background = (m === mode) ? '#1e1b4b' : '#e2e8f0';
      el.style.color = (m === mode) ? '#fff' : '#1e293b';
    }
  });

  const sl1 = document.getElementById('slParam1');
  const sl2 = document.getElementById('slParam2');
  const sl3 = document.getElementById('slParam3');

  if (mode === 'piston') {
    document.getElementById('lblParam1Title').textContent = 'Crank Radius r_OA:';
    sl1.min = 0.10; sl1.max = 0.22; sl1.step = 0.01; sl1.value = 0.15;
    document.getElementById('lblParam2Title').textContent = 'Crank Speed ω_OA:';
    sl2.min = 2; sl2.max = 25; sl2.step = 1; sl2.value = 10;
    document.getElementById('lblParam3Title').textContent = 'Crank Angle θ:';
    sl3.min = 0; sl3.max = 360; sl3.step = 1; sl3.value = 45;
    animAngle = 45;
  } else if (mode === 'bar') {
    document.getElementById('lblParam1Title').textContent = 'Ladder Length L:';
    sl1.min = 4.0; sl1.max = 12.0; sl1.step = 0.5; sl1.value = 10.0;
    document.getElementById('lblParam2Title').textContent = 'Top Slide Speed v_A (↓):';
    sl2.min = 1.0; sl2.max = 6.0; sl2.step = 0.5; sl2.value = 3.0;
    document.getElementById('lblParam3Title').textContent = 'Floor Angle θ:';
    sl3.min = 18; sl3.max = 78; sl3.step = 1; sl3.value = 60;
    animAngle = 60;
  } else if (mode === 'wheel') {
    document.getElementById('lblParam1Title').textContent = 'Wheel Radius R:';
    sl1.min = 0.20; sl1.max = 0.80; sl1.step = 0.05; sl1.value = 0.40;
    document.getElementById('lblParam2Title').textContent = 'Center Speed v_G:';
    sl2.min = 0.50; sl2.max = 5.00; sl2.step = 0.25; sl2.value = 2.00;
    document.getElementById('lblParam3Title').textContent = 'Rim Angle θ (from Top):';
    sl3.min = 0; sl3.max = 360; sl3.step = 1; sl3.value = 60;
    animAngle = 60;
    wheelXOffset = 0;
  } else if (mode === 'spool') {
    document.getElementById('lblParam1Title').textContent = 'Disk Radius r:';
    sl1.min = 3.0; sl1.max = 10.0; sl1.step = 0.5; sl1.value = 6.0;
    document.getElementById('lblParam2Title').textContent = 'Unwind Speed ω_d:';
    sl2.min = 5; sl2.max = 30; sl2.step = 1; sl2.value = 20;
    document.getElementById('lblParam3Title').textContent = 'Rotation Angle φ:';
    sl3.min = 0; sl3.max = 360; sl3.step = 1; sl3.value = 45;
    animAngle = 45;
    spoolYOffset = 0;
  }
  drawICCanvas();
}

function toggleICAnim() {
  isPlaying = !isPlaying;
  const btn = document.getElementById('btnAnim');
  if (isPlaying) {
    btn.textContent = '⏸ Pause Motion';
    btn.style.background = '#d97706';
    animAngle = parseFloat(document.getElementById('slParam3').value);
    let lastTime = performance.now();
    function step(now) {
      if (!isPlaying) return;
      const dt = Math.min((now - lastTime) / 1000, 0.08);
      lastTime = now;
      const sl3 = document.getElementById('slParam3');
      if (icMode === 'piston') {
        const w = parseFloat(document.getElementById('slParam2').value);
        animAngle = (animAngle + w * dt * 10) % 360;
        sl3.value = Math.round(animAngle);
      } else if (icMode === 'bar') {
        const vA = parseFloat(document.getElementById('slParam2').value);
        animAngle = animAngle - (10 + vA * 4) * dt;
        if (animAngle < 18) animAngle = 78;
        sl3.value = Math.round(animAngle);
      } else if (icMode === 'wheel') {
        const R = parseFloat(document.getElementById('slParam1').value);
        const vG = parseFloat(document.getElementById('slParam2').value);
        const omega = vG / R;
        wheelXOffset = (wheelXOffset + vG * dt * 38) % 220;
        animAngle = (animAngle + (omega * dt * 180 / Math.PI) * 0.55) % 360;
        sl3.value = Math.round(animAngle);
      } else if (icMode === 'spool') {
        const wd = parseFloat(document.getElementById('slParam2').value);
        animAngle = (animAngle + wd * dt * 4.5) % 360;
        spoolYOffset = (spoolYOffset + wd * dt * 2.2) % 95;
        sl3.value = Math.round(animAngle);
      }
      drawICCanvas();
      icAnimId = requestAnimationFrame(step);
    }
    icAnimId = requestAnimationFrame(step);
  } else {
    btn.textContent = '▶ Play Motion';
    btn.style.background = '#059669';
    if (icAnimId) cancelAnimationFrame(icAnimId);
  }
}

function drawVec(ctx, x1, y1, x2, y2, color, label, offsetX=8, offsetY=-6) {
  const dx = x2 - x1, dy = y2 - y1;
  const len = Math.hypot(dx, dy);
  if (len < 2) return;
  const angle = Math.atan2(dy, dx);
  const head = 9;
  ctx.save();
  ctx.strokeStyle = color;
  ctx.fillStyle = color;
  ctx.lineWidth = 2.6;
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.moveTo(x1, y1);
  ctx.lineTo(x2, y2);
  ctx.stroke();

  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.moveTo(x2, y2);
  ctx.lineTo(x2 - head * Math.cos(angle - Math.PI / 6), y2 - head * Math.sin(angle - Math.PI / 6));
  ctx.lineTo(x2 - head * Math.cos(angle + Math.PI / 6), y2 - head * Math.sin(angle + Math.PI / 6));
  ctx.closePath();
  ctx.fill();

  if (label) {
    ctx.font = 'bold 12px "Computer Modern Serif", Georgia, serif';
    ctx.fillText(label, x2 + offsetX, y2 + offsetY);
  }
  ctx.restore();
}

function drawICCanvas() {
  const cv = document.getElementById('cvICZV');
  if (!cv) return;
  const ctx = cv.getContext('2d');
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, cv.width, cv.height);

  ctx.strokeStyle = '#f1f5f9';
  ctx.lineWidth = 1;
  for (let x = 20; x < cv.width; x += 20) {
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x, 0); ctx.lineTo(x, cv.height); ctx.stroke();
  }
  for (let y = 20; y < cv.height; y += 20) {
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(0, y); ctx.lineTo(cv.width, y); ctx.stroke();
  }

  const p1 = parseFloat(document.getElementById('slParam1').value);
  const p2 = parseFloat(document.getElementById('slParam2').value);
  const p3 = isPlaying ? animAngle : parseFloat(document.getElementById('slParam3').value);

  if (icMode === 'piston') {
    const r = p1;
    const L = 0.45;
    const wOA = p2;
    const thetaDeg = Math.round(p3);
    const theta = p3 * Math.PI / 180;

    document.getElementById('lblParam1Val').textContent = r.toFixed(2) + ' m';
    document.getElementById('lblParam2Val').textContent = wOA.toFixed(1) + ' rad/s';
    document.getElementById('lblParam3Val').textContent = thetaDeg + '°';

    // Positioned so IC fits cleanly inside the canvas for most angles
    const ox = 115, oy = 185;
    const scale = 285;

    const ax = ox + r * Math.cos(theta) * scale;
    const ay = oy - r * Math.sin(theta) * scale;

    const sinBeta = (r / L) * Math.sin(theta);
    const cosBeta = Math.sqrt(1 - sinBeta * sinBeta);
    const xB = r * Math.cos(theta) + L * cosBeta;
    const bx = ox + xB * scale;
    const by = oy;

    ctx.strokeStyle = '#64748b';
    ctx.lineWidth = 2.5;
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.moveTo(ox + 75, oy - 22); ctx.lineTo(540, oy - 22);
    ctx.moveTo(ox + 75, oy + 22); ctx.lineTo(540, oy + 22);
    ctx.stroke();

    ctx.save();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#cbd5e1';
    ctx.setLineDash([8, 4]);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(35, oy); ctx.lineTo(550, oy); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.restore();

    ctx.save();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#cbd5e1';
    ctx.lineWidth = 1.4;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(ox, oy, r * scale, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.restore();

    const vA = wOA * r;
    const tanTheta = Math.tan(theta);
    const cosTheta = Math.cos(theta);
    const sinTheta = Math.sin(theta);

    const wAB = -(wOA * r * cosTheta) / (L * cosBeta);
    const vB = -wOA * r * sinTheta + wAB * L * sinBeta;

    const yIC_phys = xB * tanTheta;
    const icX = bx;
    const icY = oy - yIC_phys * scale;

    if (Math.abs(cosTheta) > 0.08) {
      ctx.save();
      ctx.strokeStyle = '#4338ca';
      ctx.lineWidth = 1.7;
      ctx.setLineDash([5, 4]);
      const clampedIcY = Math.max(18, Math.min(332, icY));
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(ox, oy); ctx.lineTo(icX, clampedIcY); ctx.stroke();
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(bx, by); ctx.lineTo(icX, clampedIcY); ctx.stroke();
      ctx.restore();

      ctx.fillStyle = '#dc2626';
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(icX, clampedIcY, 5.5, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill();
      ctx.font = 'bold 12px "Computer Modern Serif", Georgia, serif';
      const icLabel = (icY >= 18 && icY <= 332) ? 'IC (Rod AB)' : 'IC (To ∞)';
      ctx.fillText(icLabel, icX - 38, clampedIcY < oy ? clampedIcY - 8 : clampedIcY + 15);
    }

    ctx.fillStyle = '#dbeafe';
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#1e3a8a';
    ctx.lineWidth = 2;
    ctx.fillRect(bx - 24, by - 17, 48, 34);
    ctx.strokeRect(bx - 24, by - 17, 48, 34);

    ctx.strokeStyle = '#312e81';
    ctx.lineWidth = 6;
    ctx.lineCap = 'round';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(ox, oy); ctx.lineTo(ax, ay); ctx.stroke();

    ctx.strokeStyle = '#1e1b4b';
    ctx.lineWidth = 5;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(ax, ay); ctx.lineTo(bx, by); ctx.stroke();

    ctx.fillStyle = '#0f172a';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(ox, oy, 5, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill();
    ctx.fillStyle = '#2563eb';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(ax, ay, 5, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill();
    ctx.fillStyle = '#059669';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(bx, by, 5, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill();

    ctx.font = 'bold 12px "Computer Modern Serif", Georgia, serif';
    ctx.fillStyle = '#0f172a';
    ctx.fillText('O', ox - 16, oy + 15);
    ctx.fillText('A', ax - 14, ay - 8);
    ctx.fillText('B', bx - 5, by + 33);

    const vScale = 24;
    const vAx = -vA * sinTheta, vAy = -vA * cosTheta;
    drawVec(ctx, ax, ay, ax + vAx * vScale, ay + vAy * vScale, '#2563eb', `vA = ${vA.toFixed(2)} m/s`, 6, -6);
    if (Math.abs(vB) > 0.03) {
      drawVec(ctx, bx, by, bx + vB * vScale, by, '#059669', `vB = ${Math.abs(vB).toFixed(2)} m/s`, -22, -22);
    }

    const rAIC = Math.hypot(xB - r * cosTheta, yIC_phys - r * sinTheta);
    const rBIC = Math.abs(yIC_phys);

    document.getElementById('icInsightBox').innerHTML =
      `<strong>Horizontal Piston Kinematics:</strong> Since <strong>v</strong><sub>A</sub> &perp; <em>OA</em>, the normal ray at <em>A</em> is the extension of crank line <em>OA</em>. The normal to horizontal piston velocity <strong>v</strong><sub>B</sub> is a vertical line at <em>B</em>. At <em>&theta; = 90&deg;, 270&deg;</em>, the normals are parallel (<em>&omega;<sub>AB</sub> = 0</em>).`;

    document.getElementById('icReadout').innerHTML = `
      <div><span style="color:#94a3b8;">Crank Pin v_A:</span> <strong>${vA.toFixed(2)} m/s</strong></div>
      <div><span style="color:#c4b5fd;">Rod ω_AB:</span> <strong>${Math.abs(wAB).toFixed(2)} rad/s</strong></div>
      <div><span style="color:#6ee7b7;">Piston v_B (x-dir):</span> <strong>${vB.toFixed(2)} m/s</strong></div>
      <div><span style="color:#fcd34d;">Radii r_A / r_B:</span> <strong>${(rAIC > 9 ? '∞' : rAIC.toFixed(2)+'m')} / ${(rBIC > 9 ? '∞' : rBIC.toFixed(2)+'m')}</strong></div>
    `;
  } else if (icMode === 'bar') {
    const L = p1;
    const vA = p2;
    const phiDeg = Math.round(p3);
    const phi = p3 * Math.PI / 180;

    document.getElementById('lblParam1Val').textContent = L.toFixed(1) + ' ft';
    document.getElementById('lblParam2Val').textContent = vA.toFixed(1) + ' ft/s';
    document.getElementById('lblParam3Val').textContent = phiDeg + '°';

    const wallX = 115;
    const floorY = 295;
    const pxL = 130 + L * 8;

    const ax = wallX;
    const ay = floorY - pxL * Math.sin(phi);
    const bx = wallX + pxL * Math.cos(phi);
    const by = floorY;
    const icX = bx;
    const icY = ay;

    ctx.save();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#e2e8f0';
    ctx.lineWidth = 1.6;
    ctx.setLineDash([4, 4]);
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.arc(wallX, floorY, pxL, -Math.PI/2, 0);
    ctx.stroke();
    ctx.restore();

    ctx.strokeStyle = '#0f172a';
    ctx.lineWidth = 3;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(wallX, 30); ctx.lineTo(wallX, floorY); ctx.lineTo(500, floorY); ctx.stroke();

    ctx.save();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#4338ca';
    ctx.lineWidth = 1.8;
    ctx.setLineDash([6, 4]);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(ax, ay); ctx.lineTo(icX, icY); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(bx, by); ctx.lineTo(icX, icY); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.restore();

    ctx.strokeStyle = '#1e1b4b';
    ctx.lineWidth = 6;
    ctx.lineCap = 'round';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(ax, ay); ctx.lineTo(bx, by); ctx.stroke();

    const rAIC = L * Math.cos(phi);
    const rBIC = L * Math.sin(phi);
    const omega = vA / rAIC;
    const vB = omega * rBIC;

    const vScale = 14;
    drawVec(ctx, ax, ay, ax, ay + vA * vScale, '#2563eb', `vA = ${vA.toFixed(2)} ft/s`, -92, 12);
    drawVec(ctx, bx, by, bx + vB * vScale, by, '#059669', `vB = ${vB.toFixed(2)} ft/s`, 8, -8);

    ctx.fillStyle = '#2563eb';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(ax, ay, 5, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill();
    ctx.fillText('A', ax - 18, ay + 4);

    ctx.fillStyle = '#059669';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(bx, by, 5, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill();
    ctx.fillText('B', bx - 4, by + 18);

    ctx.fillStyle = '#dc2626';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(icX, icY, 5.5, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill();
    ctx.fillText('ICZV (v = 0)', icX + 10, icY + 4);

    document.getElementById('icInsightBox').innerHTML =
      `<strong>Sliding Ladder Geometry:</strong> With floor angle <em>&theta; = ${phiDeg}&deg;</em>, horizontal distance <em>r<sub>A/IC</sub> = L cos &theta; = ${rAIC.toFixed(2)} ft</em> and vertical distance <em>r<sub>B/IC</sub> = L sin &theta; = ${rBIC.toFixed(2)} ft</em>.`;

    document.getElementById('icReadout').innerHTML = `
      <div><span style="color:#94a3b8;">Angular Speed ω:</span> <strong>${omega.toFixed(2)} rad/s (CCW)</strong></div>
      <div><span style="color:#c4b5fd;">r_(A/IC) / r_(B/IC):</span> <strong>${rAIC.toFixed(2)} / ${rBIC.toFixed(2)} ft</strong></div>
      <div><span style="color:#93c5fd;">Wall Speed v_A:</span> <strong>${vA.toFixed(2)} ft/s (↓)</strong></div>
      <div><span style="color:#6ee7b7;">Floor Speed v_B:</span> <strong>${vB.toFixed(2)} ft/s (→)</strong></div>
    `;
  } else if (icMode === 'wheel') {
    const R = p1;
    const vG = p2;
    const thetaDeg = Math.round(p3);
    const theta = p3 * Math.PI / 180;
    const omega = vG / R;

    document.getElementById('lblParam1Val').textContent = R.toFixed(2) + ' m';
    document.getElementById('lblParam2Val').textContent = vG.toFixed(2) + ' m/s';
    document.getElementById('lblParam3Val').textContent = thetaDeg + '°';

    const groundY = 290;
    const pxRadius = 55 + R * 75;
    const cx = 165 + wheelXOffset;
    const cy = groundY - pxRadius;

    ctx.strokeStyle = '#0f172a';
    ctx.lineWidth = 3;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(30, groundY); ctx.lineTo(540, groundY); ctx.stroke();

    ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(238, 242, 255, 0.85)';
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#1e1b4b';
    ctx.lineWidth = 2.6;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(cx, cy, pxRadius, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();

    ctx.strokeStyle = '#cbd5e1';
    ctx.lineWidth = 1.4;
    for (let s = 0; s < 4; s++) {
      const ang = theta + s * Math.PI / 2;
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.moveTo(cx - pxRadius * Math.sin(ang), cy + pxRadius * Math.cos(ang));
      ctx.lineTo(cx + pxRadius * Math.sin(ang), cy - pxRadius * Math.cos(ang));
      ctx.stroke();
    }

    const icX = cx, icY = groundY;
    const pX = cx + pxRadius * Math.sin(theta);
    const pY = cy - pxRadius * Math.cos(theta);

    ctx.save();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#4338ca';
    ctx.lineWidth = 2;
    ctx.setLineDash([6, 4]);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(icX, icY); ctx.lineTo(pX, pY); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(icX, icY); ctx.lineTo(cx, cy); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.restore();

    const rPIC = 2 * R * Math.cos(theta / 2);
    const vP = omega * Math.abs(rPIC);
    const vScale = 22;
    drawVec(ctx, cx, cy, cx + vG * vScale, cy, '#2563eb', `vG = ${vG.toFixed(2)} m/s`, 8, -6);

    const rx = pX - icX, ry = pY - icY;
    const rLen = Math.hypot(rx, ry);
    if (rLen > 2) {
      const ux = -ry / rLen, uy = rx / rLen;
      drawVec(ctx, pX, pY, pX + ux * vP * vScale, pY + uy * vP * vScale, '#059669', `vP = ${vP.toFixed(2)} m/s`, 8, -6);
    }

    ctx.fillStyle = '#dc2626';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(icX, icY, 5.5, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill();
    ctx.font = 'bold 12px "Computer Modern Serif", Georgia, serif';
    ctx.fillText('IC (v = 0)', icX - 24, icY + 22);

    ctx.fillStyle = '#059669';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(pX, pY, 4.5, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill();
    ctx.fillText('P', pX - 14, pY - 6);

    document.getElementById('icInsightBox').innerHTML =
      `<strong>No-Slip Rolling Wheel:</strong> Ground contact point has <strong>v</strong><sub>IC</sub> = <strong>0</strong>, so <em>&omega; = v<sub>G</sub> / R</em> and any rim point moves perpendicular to chord <em>IC&ndash;P</em>.`;

    document.getElementById('icReadout').innerHTML = `
      <div><span style="color:#94a3b8;">Angular Speed ω:</span> <strong>${omega.toFixed(2)} rad/s (CW)</strong></div>
      <div><span style="color:#c4b5fd;">Chord r_(P/IC):</span> <strong>${Math.abs(rPIC).toFixed(3)} m</strong></div>
      <div><span style="color:#93c5fd;">Center v_G:</span> <strong>${vG.toFixed(2)} m/s</strong></div>
      <div><span style="color:#6ee7b7;">Rim Speed v_P:</span> <strong>${vP.toFixed(2)} m/s</strong></div>
    `;
  } else if (icMode === 'spool') {
    const r_in = p1;
    const r_ft = r_in / 12.0;
    const wd = p2;
    const phiDeg = Math.round(p3);
    const phi = p3 * Math.PI / 180;

    document.getElementById('lblParam1Val').textContent = r_in.toFixed(1) + ' in.';
    document.getElementById('lblParam2Val').textContent = wd.toFixed(0) + ' rad/s';
    document.getElementById('lblParam3Val').textContent = phiDeg + '°';

    const pxR = 45 + r_in * 5;
    const cx = 250;
    const cy = 135 + spoolYOffset;
    const ex = cx + pxR, ey = cy;

    ctx.fillStyle = '#cbd5e1';
    ctx.fillRect(ex - 35, 16, 70, 14);
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#0f172a';
    ctx.lineWidth = 2;
    ctx.strokeRect(ex - 35, 16, 70, 14);

    ctx.strokeStyle = '#92400e';
    ctx.lineWidth = 4;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(ex, 30); ctx.lineTo(ex, ey); ctx.stroke();

    ctx.fillStyle = '#eef2ff';
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#1e1b4b';
    ctx.lineWidth = 2.6;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(cx, cy, pxR, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();

    ctx.strokeStyle = '#94a3b8';
    ctx.lineWidth = 1.6;
    for (let s = 0; s < 4; s++) {
      const ang = -phi + s * Math.PI / 2;
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.moveTo(cx - pxR * Math.cos(ang), cy + pxR * Math.sin(ang));
      ctx.lineTo(cx + pxR * Math.cos(ang), cy - pxR * Math.sin(ang));
      ctx.stroke();
    }

    ctx.fillStyle = '#ffffff';
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#1e1b4b';
    ctx.lineWidth = 2;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(cx, cy, 18, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();

    const ax = cx, ay = cy - pxR;
    const bx = cx - pxR, by = cy;
    const c_x = cx, c_y = cy + pxR;

    const px = cx + pxR * Math.cos(phi);
    const py = cy - pxR * Math.sin(phi);

    ctx.save();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#4338ca';
    ctx.lineWidth = 1.6;
    ctx.setLineDash([5, 4]);
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.moveTo(ex, ey); ctx.lineTo(ax, ay);
    ctx.moveTo(ex, ey); ctx.lineTo(bx, by);
    ctx.moveTo(ex, ey); ctx.lineTo(px, py);
    ctx.stroke();
    ctx.restore();

    const vO = wd * r_ft;
    const vB = wd * (2 * r_ft);
    const vAC = wd * (Math.SQRT2 * r_ft);

    drawVec(ctx, cx, cy, cx, cy + 44, '#2563eb', `vO = ${vO.toFixed(1)} ft/s`, -85, 15);
    drawVec(ctx, bx, by, bx, by + 76, '#059669', `vB = ${vB.toFixed(1)} ft/s`, -88, 12);
    drawVec(ctx, ax, ay, ax - 36, ay + 36, '#d97706', `|vA| = ${vAC.toFixed(1)} ft/s`, -95, -6);

    ctx.fillStyle = '#7c3aed';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(px, py, 5, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill();

    ctx.fillStyle = '#dc2626';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(ex, ey, 6, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill();
    ctx.font = 'bold 12px "Computer Modern Serif", Georgia, serif';
    ctx.fillText('E = IC (v = 0)', ex + 10, ey + 4);
    ctx.fillStyle = '#0f172a';
    ctx.fillText('D (Fixed)', ex + 10, 44);
    ctx.fillText('O', cx - 15, cy - 6);
    ctx.fillText('A', ax - 5, ay - 10);
    ctx.fillText('B', bx - 18, by - 6);
    ctx.fillText('C', c_x - 16, c_y + 18);

    document.getElementById('icInsightBox').innerHTML =
      `<strong>Unwinding Disk on Stationary Rope:</strong> Because rope <em>DE</em> is attached to fixed support <em>D</em>, tangency point <em>E</em> has <strong>v</strong><sub>E</sub> = <strong>0</strong> (<em>IC</em>). Thus <em>r<sub>O/E</sub> = r</em>, <em>r<sub>B/E</sub> = 2r</em>, and <em>r<sub>A/E</sub> = r<sub>C/E</sub> = &radic;2 r</em>.`;

    document.getElementById('icReadout').innerHTML = `
      <div><span style="color:#94a3b8;">Center v_O:</span> <strong>-${vO.toFixed(2)} j ft/s</strong></div>
      <div><span style="color:#6ee7b7;">Left Rim v_B:</span> <strong>-${vB.toFixed(2)} j ft/s</strong></div>
      <div><span style="color:#fcd34d;">Top Rim v_A:</span> <strong>-${vO.toFixed(1)}i - ${vO.toFixed(1)}j ft/s</strong></div>
      <div><span style="color:#c4b5fd;">Bottom Rim v_C:</span> <strong>+${vO.toFixed(1)}i - ${vO.toFixed(1)}j ft/s</strong></div>
    `;
  }
}
if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
  document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', drawICCanvas);
} else {
  drawICCanvas();
}
</script>
```

## 4. Comprehensive Worked Examples {#worked-examples}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## ⚙️ Example 1: Fixed-Axis Disk Rotation (Variable & Constant $\alpha$)

:::: {.example-split}
::: {}
#### Problem 1A: Variable Angular Velocity

The angular velocity of a disk of radius $r = 0.8\text{ m}$ is defined by $\omega(t) = (5t^2 + 2)\text{ rad/s}$, where $t$ is in seconds. Determine the magnitudes of the velocity and total acceleration of point $A$ on the outer edge of the disk when $t = 0.5\text{ s}$.
:::

::: {.svg-frame}
```{=html}
<svg class="tikz-svg" viewBox="0 0 260 190" width="100%" height="165" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<circle cx="115" cy="95" r="68" fill="#ffedd5" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="2"/>
<circle cx="115" cy="95" r="9" fill="#d6d3d1" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<line x1="115" y1="95" x2="165" y2="49" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrK)"/>
<circle cx="165" cy="49" r="4" fill="#0f172a"/>
<text x="160" y="38" font-size="14" font-style="italic" font-weight="bold">A</text>
<rect x="132" y="69" width="38" height="16" rx="2" fill="#ffedd5"/>
<text x="151" y="81" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">0.8 m</text>
<path d="M 192 128 A 78 78 0 0 0 192 62" fill="none" stroke="#0284c7" stroke-width="2.2" marker-end="url(#arrB)"/>
<text x="200" y="99" font-size="13" font-style="italic" font-weight="bold" fill="#0284c7">ω(t)</text>
</svg>
```
:::
::::

1. **Evaluate $\omega$ and $\alpha = \dfrac{d\omega}{dt}$ at $t = 0.5\text{ s}$:**
   $$\omega(0.5) = 5(0.5)^2 + 2 = \mathbf{3.25\text{ rad/s}}, \qquad \alpha(0.5) = \frac{d}{dt}(5t^2+2)\Big|_{t=0.5} = 10(0.5) = \mathbf{5.00\text{ rad/s}^2}$$
2. **Linear Speed and Orthogonal Acceleration Components:**
   $$v_A = \omega r = (3.25)(0.8) = \mathbf{2.60\text{ m/s}}$$
   $$a_t = \alpha r = (5.00)(0.8) = 4.00\text{ m/s}^2, \qquad a_n = \omega^2 r = (3.25)^2(0.8) = 8.45\text{ m/s}^2$$
   $$a_A = \sqrt{a_t^2 + a_n^2} = \sqrt{(4.00)^2 + (8.45)^2} = \mathbf{9.35\text{ m/s}^2}$$

---

:::: {.example-split}
::: {}
#### Problem 1B: Constant Angular Acceleration (Points $A$ & $B$)

A disk is originally rotating at $\omega_0 = 8\text{ rad/s}$ and is subjected to a constant angular acceleration $\alpha = 6\text{ rad/s}^2$:

* **Part (i):** Find the velocity and normal/tangential acceleration components of outer point $A$ ($r_A = 2\text{ ft}$) at $t = 0.5\text{ s}$.
* **Part (ii):** Find the velocity and acceleration components of inner point $B$ ($r_B = 1.5\text{ ft}$) just after the wheel undergoes 2 complete revolutions ($\Delta\theta = 4\pi\text{ rad}$).
:::

::: {.svg-frame}
```{=html}
<svg class="tikz-svg" viewBox="0 0 280 200" width="100%" height="175" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<circle cx="122" cy="108" r="68" fill="#ccfbf1" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="2"/>
<polygon points="110,128 122,108 134,128" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<rect x="94" y="128" width="56" height="8" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<line x1="82" y1="136" x2="162" y2="136" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="2"/>
<line x1="122" y1="108" x2="190" y2="108" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrK)"/>
<circle cx="190" cy="108" r="4" fill="#0f172a"/>
<text x="198" y="112" font-size="13" font-style="italic" font-weight="bold">A</text>
<rect x="143" y="90" width="28" height="14" rx="2" fill="#ccfbf1"/>
<text x="157" y="101" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">2 ft</text>
<line x1="122" y1="108" x2="86" y2="72" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrK)"/>
<circle cx="86" cy="72" r="4" fill="#0f172a"/>
<text x="74" y="67" font-size="13" font-style="italic" font-weight="bold">B</text>
<rect x="68" y="86" width="34" height="15" rx="2" fill="#ccfbf1"/>
<text x="85" y="97" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">1.5 ft</text>
<path d="M 140 31 A 78 78 0 0 1 186 62" fill="none" stroke="#0284c7" stroke-width="2.2" marker-end="url(#arrB)"/>
<text x="176" y="27" font-size="12" font-style="italic" font-weight="bold" fill="#0f172a">ω<tspan dy="3" font-size="8.5" font-style="normal">0</tspan><tspan dy="-3" font-style="normal"> = 8 rad/s</tspan></text>
</svg>
```
:::
::::

* **Part (i) Point $A$ at $t = 0.5\text{ s}$:**
  $$\begin{aligned}
  \omega &= \omega_0 + \alpha t = 8 + 6(0.5) = \mathbf{11.0\text{ rad/s}} \\
  v_A &= \omega r_A = (11)(2) = \mathbf{22.0\text{ ft/s}} \\
  (a_A)_t &= \alpha r_A = (6)(2) = \mathbf{12.0\text{ ft/s}^2}, \qquad (a_A)_n = \omega^2 r_A = (11)^2(2) = \mathbf{242\text{ ft/s}^2}
  \end{aligned}$$

* **Part (ii) Point $B$ after $\Delta\theta = 2\text{ rev} = 4\pi\text{ rad}$:**
  $$\begin{aligned}
  \omega^2 &= \omega_0^2 + 2\alpha\Delta\theta = 8^2 + 2(6)(4\pi) = 214.80 \implies \omega = \mathbf{14.66\text{ rad/s}} \\
  v_B &= \omega r_B = (14.66)(1.5) = \mathbf{22.0\text{ ft/s}} \\
  (a_B)_t &= \alpha r_B = \mathbf{9.00\text{ ft/s}^2}, \qquad (a_B)_n = \omega^2 r_B = \mathbf{322\text{ ft/s}^2}
  \end{aligned}$$

## 🪜 Example 2: The Sliding Ladder (ICZV vs. Vector Algebra)

:::: {.example-split}
::: {}
#### Problem Statement

A $L = 10\text{ ft}$ ladder rests against a vertical wall. The top of the ladder (Point $A$) slides straight down the wall at a constant velocity of $v_A = 3\text{ ft/s}$. At the instant shown, the ladder makes a $\theta = 60^\circ$ angle with the horizontal floor. Determine the velocity $v_B$ of the bottom of the ladder and the angular velocity $\omega$ using both methods.
:::

::: {.svg-frame}
```{=html}
<svg class="tikz-svg" viewBox="0 0 280 210" width="100%" height="180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<polyline points="55,20 55,175 245,175" fill="none" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<line x1="55" y1="45" x2="145" y2="45" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/>
<line x1="145" y1="175" x2="145" y2="45" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/>
<line x1="55" y1="45" x2="145" y2="175" stroke="#92400e" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round"/>
<line x1="55" y1="45" x2="55" y2="95" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#arrB)"/>
<line x1="145" y1="175" x2="205" y2="175" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#arrR)"/>
<circle cx="55" cy="45" r="4" fill="#0f172a"/>
<circle cx="145" cy="175" r="4" fill="#0f172a"/>
<circle cx="145" cy="45" r="4.5" fill="#dc2626"/>
<text x="42" y="48" font-size="13" font-style="italic" font-weight="bold">A</text>
<text x="145" y="193" font-size="13" font-style="italic" font-weight="bold">B</text>
<text x="153" y="42" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#dc2626">ICZV</text>
<text x="62" y="92" font-size="11.5" font-style="italic" font-weight="bold" fill="#2563eb">v<tspan dy="3" font-size="8.5" font-style="normal">A</tspan><tspan dy="-3" font-style="normal"> = 3 ft/s</tspan></text>
<text x="185" y="166" font-size="12" font-style="italic" font-weight="bold" fill="#dc2626">v<tspan dy="3" font-size="8.5" font-style="normal">B</tspan></text>
<text x="115" y="168" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">60°</text>
<text x="100" y="36" font-size="11.5" font-style="italic" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">r<tspan dy="3" font-size="8.5" font-style="normal">A/IC</tspan></text>
<text x="154" y="115" font-size="11.5" font-style="italic" font-weight="bold">r<tspan dy="3" font-size="8.5" font-style="normal">B/IC</tspan></text>
</svg>
```
:::
::::

#### Method A: Instantaneous Center (Geometric)
1. **Locate $ICZV$:** Draw a horizontal line $\perp$ to $\mathbf{v}_A$ from $A$ and a vertical line $\perp$ to $\mathbf{v}_B$ from $B$.
2. **Radial Distances from $ICZV$:**
   $$r_{A/IC} = 10\cos(60^\circ) = 5.00\text{ ft}, \qquad r_{B/IC} = 10\sin(60^\circ) = 8.66\text{ ft}$$
3. **Solve for $\omega$ and $v_B$:**
   $$\omega = \frac{v_A}{r_{A/IC}} = \frac{3\text{ ft/s}}{5.00\text{ ft}} = \mathbf{0.60\text{ rad/s}\ (\text{CCW})}, \qquad v_B = \omega r_{B/IC} = (0.60)(8.66) = \mathbf{5.20\text{ ft/s}\ (\rightarrow)}$$

#### Method B: Relative Velocity Equation (Vector Algebra)
1. **Express Vectors:** $\mathbf{v}_A = -3\hat{\mathbf{j}}\text{ ft/s}$, $\mathbf{v}_B = v_B\hat{\mathbf{i}}$, $\boldsymbol{\omega} = \omega\hat{\mathbf{k}}$, and $\mathbf{r}_{B/A} = 5\hat{\mathbf{i}} - 8.66\hat{\mathbf{j}}\text{ ft}$.
2. **Substitute into $\mathbf{v}_B = \mathbf{v}_A + \boldsymbol{\omega} \times \mathbf{r}_{B/A}$:**
   $$v_B\hat{\mathbf{i}} = -3\hat{\mathbf{j}} + (\omega\hat{\mathbf{k}}) \times (5\hat{\mathbf{i}} - 8.66\hat{\mathbf{j}}) = 8.66\omega\hat{\mathbf{i}} + (5\omega - 3)\hat{\mathbf{j}}$$
3. **Equate Components:** $5\omega - 3 = 0 \implies \mathbf{\omega = 0.60\text{ rad/s}}$ and $v_B = 8.66(0.60) = \mathbf{5.20\text{ ft/s}}$.

## 🚗 Example 3: Horizontal Slider-Crank Piston Mechanism

:::: {.example-split}
::: {}
#### Problem Statement

In an internal combustion engine, crank $OA$ of length $r = 0.15\text{ m}$ rotates counter-clockwise at $\omega_{OA} = 10\text{ rad/s}$ at the instant $\theta = 45^\circ$. Connecting rod $AB$ has length $L = 0.45\text{ m}$, and piston $B$ is constrained to move horizontally along the $x$-axis. Determine the angular velocity $\omega_{AB}$ of the connecting rod and the horizontal velocity $v_B$ of the piston.
:::

::: {.svg-frame}
```{=html}
<svg class="tikz-svg" viewBox="0 0 300 200" width="100%" height="175" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<line x1="25" y1="155" x2="280" y2="155" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
<line x1="50" y1="155" x2="215" y2="25" stroke="#4338ca" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/>
<line x1="215" y1="155" x2="215" y2="25" stroke="#4338ca" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/>
<rect x="193" y="141" width="44" height="28" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#1e3a8a" stroke-width="2"/>
<line x1="50" y1="155" x2="95" y2="119" stroke="#312e81" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round"/>
<line x1="95" y1="119" x2="215" y2="155" stroke="#1e1b4b" stroke-width="4.5" stroke-linecap="round"/>
<circle cx="50" cy="155" r="4" fill="#0f172a"/>
<circle cx="95" cy="119" r="4" fill="#2563eb"/>
<circle cx="215" cy="155" r="4" fill="#059669"/>
<circle cx="215" cy="25" r="5" fill="#dc2626"/>
<text x="42" y="172" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">O</text>
<text x="82" y="112" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#2563eb">A</text>
<text x="212" y="184" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#059669">B (Piston)</text>
<text x="155" y="24" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#dc2626">IC (Rod AB)</text>
<text x="72" y="150" font-size="11" font-weight="bold">45°</text>
</svg>
```
:::
::::

1. **Crank Pin Velocity at $A$:**
   $$v_A = \omega_{OA} r = (10\text{ rad/s})(0.15\text{ m}) = \mathbf{1.50\text{ m/s}} \quad (\perp \text{to crank } OA)$$
2. **Connecting Rod Angle $\beta$ (Law of Sines):**
   $$\sin\beta = \frac{r\sin(45^\circ)}{L} = \frac{0.15(0.7071)}{0.45} = 0.2357 \implies \beta = 13.63^\circ, \quad \cos\beta = 0.9718$$
3. **Locate $IC$ of Connecting Rod $AB$:**
   * The line $\perp$ to $\mathbf{v}_A$ is the extension of crank $OA$ (at $45^\circ$).
   * The line $\perp$ to horizontal piston velocity $\mathbf{v}_B$ is a vertical line passing through $B$ at horizontal coordinate $x_B = r\cos(45^\circ) + L\cos\beta = 0.1061 + 0.4373 = 0.5434\text{ m}$.
   * Because the $OA$ line has slope $\tan(45^\circ) = 1$, the vertical coordinate of $IC$ is $y_{IC} = x_B \tan(45^\circ) = 0.5434\text{ m}$.
4. **Distances from $IC$ and Final Velocities:**
   $$r_{B/IC} = y_{IC} = 0.5434\text{ m}, \qquad r_{A/IC} = \sqrt{(0.5434 - 0.1061)^2 + (0.5434 - 0.1061)^2} = 0.6184\text{ m}$$
   $$\omega_{AB} = \frac{v_A}{r_{A/IC}} = \frac{1.50}{0.6184} = \mathbf{2.43\text{ rad/s}\ (\text{CW})}, \qquad v_B = \omega_{AB} r_{B/IC} = (2.425)(0.5434) = \mathbf{1.32\text{ m/s}\ (\leftarrow)}$$

:::

```{=html}
&bull; <strong>Point C:</strong> <strong>v</strong><sub>C</sub> = +10<strong>i</strong> &minus; 10<strong>j</strong> ft/s (|v<sub>C</sub>| = <strong>14.14 ft/s</strong>)
```

**Problem 2:** A heavy gate hinged at $O$ is pushed closed by car bumper $A$ at a constant horizontal distance $w = 24\text{ m}$ from $O$. If the car moves straight downward ($\downarrow$) at $v_A = 1.2\text{ m/s}$, find the angular speed $\omega$ ($\text{rad/s}$) of the gate when $\theta = 15^\circ$.

```{=html}
<div style="margin-top: 10px; display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap;">
<input type="number" id="ansP2" placeholder="ω_gate (rad/s)" step="0.001" style="padding: 6px 10px; border: 1px solid #cbd5e1; border-radius: 6px; width: 155px; font-size: 0.85rem;">
<button type="button" onclick="checkP2()" style="background: #1e1b4b; color: #fff; border: none; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 6px; font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.8rem; cursor: pointer;">Check</button>
<span id="resP2" style="font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 700;"></span>
</div>
<details style="margin-top: 10px; font-size: 0.86rem;">
<summary style="cursor: pointer; font-weight: 700; color: #4338ca;">Show Geometric &amp; Calculus Solution</summary>
<div style="padding-top: 8px; color: #334155;">
The car contact point stays at constant horizontal distance <em>w = 24 m</em>, so its vertical position is <em>y<sub>A</sub> = w tan &theta;</em>.<br>
Differentiating with respect to time:<br>
<em>&dot;y<sub>A</sub> = w sec<sup>2</sup>(&theta;) &middot; &dot;&theta; &implies; &omega; = (v<sub>A</sub> cos<sup>2</sup>&theta;) / w</em><br>
At <em>&theta; = 15&deg;</em>: <em>&omega; = 1.2 &times; cos<sup>2</sup>(15&deg;) / 24 = (1.2 &times; 0.9330) / 24 = <strong>0.0467 rad/s (CW)</strong></em>.
</div>
</details>
```

::: {.kin-card-body}
**Problem 3:** A wheel ($R = 14\text{ in.}$) rolls right with center speed $v_B = 7\text{ ft/s}$ ($84\text{ in./s}$). Bar $AB$ ($L = 40\text{ in.}$) connects center $B$ to vertical slider $A$. When $\theta = 72^\circ$, find $\omega_{AB}$ ($\text{rad/s}$) and slider speed $v_A$ ($\text{ft/s}$).

```{=html}
<div style="margin-top: 10px; display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap;">
<input type="number" id="ansP3W" placeholder="ω_AB (rad/s)" step="0.01" style="padding: 6px 10px; border: 1px solid #cbd5e1; border-radius: 6px; width: 130px; font-size: 0.85rem;">
<input type="number" id="ansP3V" placeholder="Speed |v_A| (ft/s)" step="0.1" style="padding: 6px 10px; border: 1px solid #cbd5e1; border-radius: 6px; width: 135px; font-size: 0.85rem;">
<button type="button" onclick="checkP3()" style="background: #1e1b4b; color: #fff; border: none; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 6px; font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.8rem; cursor: pointer;">Check</button>
<span id="resP3" style="font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 700;"></span>
</div>
<details style="margin-top: 10px; font-size: 0.86rem;">
<summary style="cursor: pointer; font-weight: 700; color: #4338ca;">Show ICZV &amp; Vector Solution</summary>
<div style="padding-top: 8px; color: #334155;">
Slider <em>A</em> moves vertically (&perp; ray is horizontal) and wheel center <em>B</em> moves horizontally (&perp; ray is vertical).<br>
&bull; <em>r<sub>B/IC</sub> = L sin(72&deg;) = 40(0.9511) = 38.04 in. = 3.170 ft</em><br>
&bull; <em>r<sub>A/IC</sub> = L cos(72&deg;) = 40(0.3090) = 12.36 in. = 1.030 ft</em><br>
&bull; <em>&omega;<sub>AB</sub> = v<sub>B</sub> / r<sub>B/IC</sub> = 7 ft/s / 3.170 ft = <strong>2.21 rad/s (CCW)</strong></em><br>
&bull; <em>v<sub>A</sub> = &omega;<sub>AB</sub> &middot; r<sub>A/IC</sub> = (2.208)(1.030) = <strong>2.27 ft/s (&darr;)</strong></em>
</div>
</details>
```

```{=html}
<script>
function checkP1() {
  const vb = parseFloat(document.getElementById('ansP1B').value);
  const va = parseFloat(document.getElementById('ansP1A').value);
  const res = document.getElementById('resP1');
  if (Math.abs(vb - 20) <= 0.3 && Math.abs(va - 14.14) <= 0.3) {
    res.style.color = '#059669';
    res.textContent = '✓ Correct! |v_B| = 20 ft/s, |v_A| = 14.14 ft/s';
  } else {
    res.style.color = '#dc2626';
    res.textContent = '✗ Hint: E is ICZV! r_B/E = 2r (1 ft) and r_A/E = √2 r.';
  }
}
function checkP2() {
  const w = parseFloat(document.getElementById('ansP2').value);
  const res = document.getElementById('resP2');
  if (Math.abs(w - 0.0467) <= 0.003) {
    res.style.color = '#059669';
    res.textContent = '✓ Correct! ω = 0.0467 rad/s (CW)';
  } else {
    res.style.color = '#dc2626';
    res.textContent = '✗ Hint: Use y_A = w tan(θ) → v_A = w sec²(θ) ω.';
  }
}
function checkP3() {
  const w = parseFloat(document.getElementById('ansP3W').value);
  const va = parseFloat(document.getElementById('ansP3V').value);
  const res = document.getElementById('resP3');
  if (Math.abs(w - 2.21) <= 0.08 && Math.abs(va - 2.27) <= 0.08) {
    res.style.color = '#059669';
    res.textContent = '✓ Correct! ω_AB = 2.21 rad/s, v_A = 2.27 ft/s';
  } else {
    res.style.color = '#dc2626';
    res.textContent = '✗ Hint: r_(B/IC) = L sin(72°) and r_(A/IC) = L cos(72°).';
  }
}
</script>
```
